## Shared server flags

Every `server` subcommand accepts these flags for specifying how

to connect:

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--transport <transport>` | Explicit transport type (`http` or `stdio`) |
| `
--url <url>` | HTTP MCP server URL |\n| `--access-token <token>` | Bearer access token |\n| `--oauth-access-token <token>` | OAuth
bearer access token |\n| `--refresh-token <token>` | OAuth refresh token |\n| `--client-id <id>` | OAuth client ID (used with `--
refresh-token`) |\n| `--client-secret <secret>` | OAuth client secret (used with `--refresh-token`) |\n| `--credentials-file <path
>` | Load OAuth credentials from a file created by `oauth login --credentials-out` or `oauth conformance --credentials-out` |\n| `
--header <header>` | HTTP header in `Key: Value` format (repeatable) |\n| `--client-capabilities <json>` | Client capabilities as
inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin |\n| `--command <command>` | Command for a stdio server |\n| `--args <arg...>` | Preferred
stdio command arguments |\n| `--command-args <arg>` | Legacy stdio command argument (repeatable) |\n| `-e, --env <env...>` | Stdio

environment `KEY=[REDACTED] values |
| `--cwd <path>` | Working directory for the stdio child process |

Stdio child processes
inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use\n`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones, and `--cwd` when the\n
command must run from a project directory.\nIf you pass `--transport`, the CLI validates that it matches the target flags\nyou pro

vided instead of silently inferring the transport.

ile to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine
with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects
your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, an
d decides the run with\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report
file. It records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](htt\n\n## Eval id
entity and local data\n\nRun `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK als
o accepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, whic\n\nEvery logic
al run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior
successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the project \n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run re
quest sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.res
olveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-s\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable ana
lytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.\n\n## Quick start\

n
### 1. Write a suite

Save this as `.mcpjam/evals/example.yaml`:

```yaml theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
schemaVersio

n: "2"
mode: agentWorkflow
reportingMode: standard
suite:
 id: s_notes_example
 name: Notes server
target:
 servers:

- name: notes
defaults:
 judge:
 enabled: false
 model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5
 iterations: 1
 passThreshold:

1
 validity: {}
cases:
 - id: c_reads_a_note
 title: reads the note it was asked about
 steps:
 - id: s1

kind: prompt
 prompt: What does note 7 say?
 - id: a1
 kind: assert
 assertion:
 type:

toolCalledAtLeastOnce
 toolName: read_note
 - id: c_never_deletes
 title: never deletes when only asked to read

steps:
 - id: s1
 kind: prompt
 prompt: Summarize note 7.
 - id: a1
 kind: assert

assertion:
 type: toolNeverCalled
 toolName: delete_note
```

`mcpjam cloud eval validate --file .mcpjam/e

vals/example.yaml` checks the file offline, with no account.

### 2. Configure the server

`mcpjam test` binds each `target.se
rvers[].name` to a local MCP config. The simplest is a `.mcp.json` next to where you run the command:\n\n```json theme={\"theme\":

me={"theme":"css-variables"}
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED]
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml
```

### 4. Fail
one on purpose, then rerun it\n\nChange `toolName: read_note` to `toolName: echo` in the first case and run again: the command exi
ts `1` and names the failing assertion. Fix it, then rerun just that case and keep a report:\n\n```bash theme={\"theme\":\"css-var

iables"}
mcpjam test .mcpjam/evals/example.yaml --case c_reads_a_note --reporter junit-xml --out reports/local.xml
```

`--ca

se` takes the exact authored id and is repeatable.

## Server bindings

For each target server name, the first source with an
entry wins; the whole entry, never a field-level merge:\n\n1. `--server <name>=<url>` (repeatable; HTTP(S) only). For a suite with
exactly one target, `--url` / `--command` and their auth flags bind it instead.\n2. `--mcp-config <path>`: an explicit MCP JSON c

onfig. A missing or invalid explicit file fails setup.
3. `./.mcp.json`
4. `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`

Paths are relative to the dir
ectory you run the command in, not to the suite file. An explicit `--mcp-config` can bind some servers while the two conventional
files still supply the rest. A lower-precedence file is read \n\nConfig entries use the standard `mcpServers` shape (`command`/`ar
gs`/`env`/`cwd` for stdio, `url`/`headers` for HTTP, with `type`/`transport` spellings such as `stdio`, `http`, `sse`, `streamable
-http`). `${VAR}` and `${\n\nOne credential is never shared across servers: servers that need their own auth each get their own co

nfig entry.

## Inference

| `--inference` | Model id | Rail |
| - | - | - |
| `auto` (default) | `provider/model` and the p
rovider's key is set | BYOK |\n| `auto` | `provider/model`, no key | MCPJam, when it serves the model and you are signed in |\n| `
auto` or `mcpjam` | `mcpjam/provider/model` | MCPJam |\n| `byok` | `mcpjam/…` | refused: the prefix is explicit routing intent |\n
| `byok` | `provider/model` | BYOK; the provider key is required |\n| `mcpjam` | `provider/model` | MCPJam; the model must be one
MCPJam serves |\n\nThere is no fallback: a key the provider rejects is a credential failure (exit `3`), never a reason to spend pl
atform credits instead.\n\nBYOK keys are read from the standard variables: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATI
VE_AI_API_KEY` (or `GEMINI_API_KEY`), `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`. `AN\n\nMCPJam-ho
